en.title: Rearrange Both Parts into Palindromes After Deleting At Most One Character Each
en.description:
Cut a lowercase string into two non-empty contiguous substrings. From each part you may delete at most one character, then rearrange it freely; output YES if both parts can form palindromes, otherwise NO. Deleting is optional, and a part of length 1 can be kept as is.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: One line containing the string. 1≤length≤300000, lowercase letters.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are YES, NO and NO. However abcde is split, one of the two parts has at least 3 characters that each occur once, so even after one deletion it cannot be rearranged into a palindrome.
hints: Maintain 26-bit parity masks of character frequencies for the whole string and for each prefix ending at a cut. If some cut leaves both sides with at most 2 odd-frequency characters, output YES; otherwise NO.
